notes: bot v7: single-instance lock now verifies the lock owner's identity before honoring the lock. The v4-v6 lock only kill(pid,0)-checked the recorded pid; on device the recorded pid was recycled by an unrelated long-lived chroot process, so every watchdog respawn exited as 'already running' while no bot was alive. The lock payload is now JSON {pid, start} (legacy bare-pid locks still parse); a recorded owner is honored only if /proc/<pid>/cmdline has argv[0] containing node plus an argument exactly equal to the bot.js path, and the recorded /proc/<pid>/stat starttime (field 22) matches when present. Foreign, recycled, dead or unparsable locks are taken over with a '锁残留（pid X 非机器人进程），接管' log line; alive-but-unverifiable owners still conservatively block, and a genuine second instance still exits with '已有实例在运行'. All other bot behavior unchanged from v6: ranked candidate fallthrough (up to 3 candidates tried silently; dead_source, failed, blocked, or link-less candidates are skipped for the next; the group sees one searching message plus the final link or one honest all-sources-failed reply), empty-search retry (up to 2 re-runs at ~6s gaps), 21:00-23:59 Asia/Shanghai digest poster, message_id dedup, video-over-novel pick. Scripts v7: the start_qqbot.sh OneBot-config seeding for the new bot account 411649762 is now self-healing. The account's first login predated the v6 seeding hook, so NapCat generated its own default onebot11_411649762.json with the WS server off, and the v6 hook's never-overwrite rule preserved that broken file ever since — NapCat logged in and received group messages while bot.js looped on '正在连接 NapCat' and port 3001 never listened. The hook now health-checks an existing per-account config at stack start (it must match ws enable:true and port 3001): healthy files are left completely untouched (legitimate per-account variation respected), unhealthy or unreadable ones are backed up to onebot11_411649762.json.bak (overwriting any previous backup) and realigned to the base onebot11.json; missing files are still seeded from base, a missing base still only warns, and no hook failure can block stack start.
